title: Pentagon video shows off dozens of F-22 Raptors to show it's 'combat ready' amid fears of WWIII
text:
The US army put its impressive power in the full exhibition when a squad from 30 lethal combat planes marched by a air force track in a training drill.
The exercise, which involved two dozen birds F-22 and six T-38 Gorons of the first combat wing of the Air Force, took place on January 31 at the base of the Langley Air Force in Virginia.
The clip captured ranks of the combat aircraft sitting on a track before spinning asphalt Groups of three strong spaced called ‘Elephant Walk’.
This is when combat airplanes are stirred and take off within 12 to 15 seconds from each other, which potentially puts a complete squad in the air in just minutes.
The camera follows to capture a powerful track of the track full of airplanes ready for war in what some believe is a message for US adversaries as tensions increase with China and Russia.
Air Force officials say that exercise serves as a reminder that the United States Army is able to display powerful planes anywhere in the world at any time.
“The exercise was carried out to demonstrate the ability of the wing to quickly deploy combat lists worldwide,” added the Air Force in a statement.
“The first FW leads the way in combat capacity and lethality worldwide, serving as the main air superiority wing in the United States.”
F-22 Raptors of the first combat wing participated in a ‘Elephant Walk’ on January 31, 2025
The ‘elephant walks’ are military exercises that practice fast take -offs for a short period of time
The video was later shared by the United States space force, the new army branch created during the first mandate of President Donald Trump.
A team of aviators recorded the imposing parade, which shows a row of F-22 aligned and ready for the flight while military helicopters look from the sky.
The exercise begins with 24 pilots of the Air Force of the first combat wing rolling in nearby formation aboard its F-22.
Subsequently, a group of T-38 Talons are joined, which are seen after the threatening group of fifth generation combat aircraft.
Near the end of the exercise, break one by one to approach the main track for minimum interval takeoff.
Since the Pentagon took over in January, the Secretary of Defense of the United States, Pete Hegseth, said his mission is to improve the mortal power of the United States Army.
Hegseth said: “Our work is lethality and preparation and war.”
“(United States) will not be a better friend for our allies and there is no stronger adversary for those who want to try and try,” he added.
Two dozen f-22 raptors
The recent strength show occurs when American meets multiple world crises and possible tense situations to treat.
Together with the threat that China exceeds US dominance in the Pacific, the United States still focuses on the invasion of Ukraine from Russia to Ukraine and the perpetually chaotic situation in the Middle East.
The Trump administration is also increasing its military presence here at home, indicating that more resources will be used to defend the southern border of the United States.
Hegseth said: “What is necessary on the border will be provided.”
‘The Department of Defense will support the defense of the territorial integrity of the southern border of the United States of America, including reservists, national guards and active duty (personal) in accordance with the constitution and laws of our land, and the directives of the managers of the commander in chief.
The F-22 has been one of the most advanced aircraft of the Air Force since the early 2000s
The stealthy nature of F-22 makes it extremely difficult for radar to detect
The video focuses on the Raptors, which can be seen aligned to the wing for wing before participating in the training exercise.
You can see a single helicopter watching the military demonstration, but it is not clear if he played a direct role in the elephant walk.
It is only the second time that the army performs this drill in Langley, and the first takes place in 2019.
As for the Air Force force show on January 31, the Pentagon chose one of its most lethal aircraft to deliver this message not so subtle.
The F-22 Raptor debuted in 2005 and was designed by Lockheed Martin to control the skies with superior technology.
The raptor birds were “the first stealthy air domain fighter,” according to the Air Force.
Their advanced stealth technology continues to make it difficult for the enemy radar to detect them, even 20 years after its debut.
The F-22 Elephant Walk video was released by the US space force after the demonstration
Bird birds of birds of birds of birds of birds of birds of birds in Europe, even in Europe, work with NATO.
Military exercise took place as global tensions continue to increase, even in Asia, Europe and the Middle East
The highly maneuverable jet can reach supersonic speeds, can trace multiple objectives simultaneously and carry a pay -guided missile load for precision, which makes it able to defend airspace, carry out recognition missions and surprising objectives anywhere.
The F-22 have already been deployed in Europe to participate in NATO exercises, since the conflict in Ukraine enters their fourth year.
The new air force video is probably the last example of Trump’s administration emphasis on ‘peace through force’, or the belief that the demonstration of superior military power will act as a deterrent element for any other nation considering The use of force.
“Together, we will ensure peace through force, and we will make the United States and the world safe again!” Then, President -elect Trump promised in 2024.
Meanwhile, the six T-38 claws that participated in the Elephant Walk currently serve as a training aircraft for the air force pilots.
Air Force notes on your website That, ‘The Air Education and Training Command uses the T-38C to prepare the pilots for the frontline fighter and the bomber aircraft such as the F-15E Strike Eagle, F-15C EAGLE, F-16 Fighting Falcon , B-1b Lancer, AA -10 Thunderbolt and F-22 Raptor.
The claws have been in service since 1959, with newer models for the test pilots that arrive in 2001.
